title: Currencies: 26 Oct 2026
key_takeaways: DXY at 104.2, marginally weaker (-0.1%) as risk appetite improved on US earnings beats; AUD/USD at 0.6482.
AUD firmed slightly on stable iron ore and equity risk-on; the pair remains capped by the RBA-Fed rate differential and China risk.
USD/JPY edged to 152.30; the BoJ is watching closely but intervention threshold is seen closer to 155.

## US dollar

The DXY edged down 0.1% to 104.20 as risk sentiment improved on strong US earnings (Microsoft, Alphabet). The dollar remains broadly supported by the interest rate differential - Fed funds at 5.25-5.50% against near-zero rates in Japan and sub-4% in Europe. The consensus view is for DXY to drift lower toward 102-103 over 12 months as the Fed begins cutting and the rate differential narrows. The key upside risk to the USD is a re-acceleration of US inflation keeping the Fed on hold.

## Australian dollar

AUD/USD at 0.6482, up 0.2% on the day. The pair is near the lower end of its 3-month range (0.6450-0.6720). Key drivers: the positive equity session (risk-on), stable iron ore above US$106/t, and the RBA hold yesterday (no surprise, no new information). The AUD/USD 0.65 level has provided support twice in October; a break would likely test 0.6420.

AUD/JPY at 98.65 - the cross is sensitive to risk sentiment and is watching the BoJ's next move. AUD/EUR at 0.5993 (just below parity), reflecting the relatively similar ECB-RBA rate path.

The consensus of major bank research (CBA, Westpac, NAB economics teams as of October 2026) is for AUD/USD to trade in the 0.64-0.68 range through H1 2027, with a gradual drift higher as the Fed cuts and commodity prices hold. The main downside risk is a China growth shock or significant iron ore price decline.

## Other majors

**EUR/USD:** 1.0815, up 0.1%. The ECB delivered its third 25bp cut of 2026 in October (deposit rate now 2.75%); markets price one more cut before year-end. EUR is broadly range-bound.

**GBP/USD:** 1.2985, up 0.3% after UK services PMI came in stronger than expected (53.2 vs 51.8 consensus), reducing near-term Bank of England cut expectations.

**USD/JPY:** 152.30, drifting toward the 155 level that BoJ officials have previously flagged as a watch point. BoJ intervention in late 2024 was triggered at 160; the current level is not seen as a trigger but the pace of move matters.

## Outlook

Consensus: USD softens gradually through 2027 as the Fed eases. AUD/USD expected to recover toward 0.68-0.70 in H2 2027 if the soft-landing thesis holds and commodity prices remain supported. EUR/USD range-bound at 1.05-1.10. The key FX risk for Australian assets is a sharper-than-expected China slowdown, which would pressure both AUD and iron ore simultaneously.
